newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

North Sydney footballers clashed with the public at a bowling club yesterday with the Bears first grade squad accused of using threatening language and intimidating bowlers who blocked their vehicles in the car park of the club. Page 46.

Brett Ogle is under scrutiny for his use of a long-handled eight-iron at Terrey Hills Club this week opening the debate over the legality of clubs not conforming with traditional gold strokes. Ogle was forced to modify the club before even stepping up for he first round of the $450,000 Canon Challenge. Page 46.

Former Wallaby captain Phil Kearn's return to the major league has been postponed for another week after being sidelines already for 18 months for an Achilles tendon injury followed by a mysterious knee ailment. Page 45.
The Bathurst city council has voted eight-five in favour of a second touring car endurance race at Mount Panorama just two weeks after the long-running Bathurst 1000 to be held on October 5. Page 45.
THE AGE

Pole vaulter Emma George set a world record last night at Olympic Park and at 4.55 metres, is now more than 32 centimetres clear of her nearest rival, the Czech Republic's Daniela Bartova. However George believes the record needs to climb a further 30 cetimetres, around 4.80 metres for the women's event to gains legitimacy. Page C8.

Tour selectors for the South African cricket tour have almost organised their preferred batting order with Matthew Elliot in number 3 position and Michael Bevan at number 7. Michael Bevan is frustrated at his role as makeshift all-rounder. Page C6.

Embattled Ian Baker-Finch is expected to make a final decision on his golfing future today after what is expected to be his final round of tournament for the game this summer. Baker-Finch shot an opening round of six-over par 78 in the Canon Challenge i Sydney in the final event of the Australasian tour and is likely to miss the cut, the 46th in his past 47 tournaments. Page C6.

Merv Hughes is set to receive an offer from Canberra that could see his cricket career extended by one more season. The ACT Cricket Association confirmed last night it was interested in the 35-year-old former Test bowler. Page C6.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian paceman Andy Bichel and Jason Gillespie will fight for a test position to partner spearhead Glenn McGrath after Paul Reiffel broke down in the Australian cricket tour match against Natal in Durban yesterday. The hamstring injury is a recurrence of one Reiffel suffered at the start of the season. Page 102.

Australian Rules player Tony McGuiness will ask the Sydney Swans to allow an independent arbitrator to rule on whether the club is liable for a damages claim after it failed to pick the former Adelaide rover up in the pre-season draft. McGuiness claims te Swans had given him a written agreement they would select him. Page 102.

Victorian pole vaulter Emma George set another world record at Olympic Park last night, easily jumping 4.55 metres at her first attempt. The jump broke George's previous record of 4.5 metres she set in the Victorian championships two weeks ago and is her10th world record. Page 104.

Geelong superstar Gary Ablett will be missing from the Cat's opening Ansett Cup match against West Coast due to a bruised knee. Also ruled out of the clash are midfielders Liam Pickering and veteran Paul Couch. Page 100.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Golfer Brett Ogle was forced to replace the grip on his chipper and replace it with tape only moments before hitting off in the first round of the Canon Challenge at Terry Hills yesterday. PGA officials found that the club, which had two grips on the shat, was illegal. Ogle scored a 73 leaving him seven strokes off the lead. Page 104.

Country race clubs will axe 127 race meetings next season in an attempt to re-vitalise the New South Wales racing industry. The two part proposal will mean only 630 race meetings will be held in 1997/98, made up of 229 TAB fixtures and 397 non-TAB fixturs. Page 104.

Peter Fortune, coach of Olympic silver medallist Cathy Freeman says "there have been a few problems" relating to the break-up of her long term partner which had adversely affected her running. Freeman has been living with her mother in Brisbane since thebreak-up but plans to compete in the Australian championships in late February. Page 102.

ST George's Warren Lockwood is considered odds-on to success Ken Arthurson as Australian Rugby League chairman next week. Lockwood is man credited with keeping the Saints in the ARL fold twice in the past 12 months when it appeared they might shift to Sperleague. Page 101.
